validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED. This is the associated-gas pipeline built with Saudi Aramco's Haradh GOSP-3 (gas-oil separation plant), commissioned Jan-Q2 2006. Two trade sources explicitly describe an associated-gas line from Haradh GOSP-3 to the 'Uthmaniyah Gas Plant: OGJ ('Aramco's Haradh GOSP-3 starts up' and 'Saudi Aramco commissions Haradh GOSP-3') and Gulf Oil & Gas ('Haradh GOSP-3 Goes Online'). All state GOSP-3 produces 300,000 b/d Arab Light + 140 MMscfd of associated gas, moved via one 1,140 hp + two 10,460 hp motor-driven gas compressors 'to transport gas by pipeline to Uthmaniyah Gas Plant.' Note the two OGJ pieces and the Gulf O&G piece likely trace to a single 2006 Aramco announcement (not fully independent origins), but the project itself is unambiguously real and heavily documented. The row's OWN wiki citations (OPEC ASB2012 p.75 and ASB2013 p.79) are generic country-level gas statistics that do NOT name this pipeline — weak/irrelevant support that on its own would be an existence flag; existence is rescued here only by the OGJ/GulfO&G GOSP-3 coverage (which is already the Start [ref]). CLASSIFICATION: defensible as a gas pipeline but note it is a field-associated-gas feeder from a GOSP to a processing plant (not an MGS sales-gas trunk); GEM consistently carries these Ghawar field-to-plant gas lines in GGIT, so keep. DUPLICATE RISK: the roster also has P1905 'Haradh-Uthmaniya Gas Pipeline' (140.01 km, 48 in) and P1917/P1918/P1919 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah' lines. P1907 (124 km, 24+32 in) and P1905 (140 km, 48 in) share the same Haradh->Uthmaniyah corridor but have different diameters and lengths; the whole P1897-P1925 cluster carries GIS-network-style segment names ('Haradh-3' = the GOSP-3 node), so these are most likely distinct network edges rather than one pipe double-counted, but a human should confirm P1905 vs P1907 are not the same physical line under two node labels. SPEC: length 124 km and diameter 24/32 in are NOT independently corroborated — sources give only 'about 160 km of new pipeline' combined to BOTH Abqaiq Stabilization Plant AND Uthmaniyah Gas Plant, so 124 km for the Uthmaniyah gas leg alone is plausible but unverified; diameter is unverified. Capacity 140 MMscfd (associated gas) IS well-sourced (see fills). GulfPub PE World Map has NO Haradh-Uthmaniyah counterpart (its SA gas roster is MGS/Qatif-Berri/Abqaiq-Qatif/East-West/Fadhili/Jafurah), so no GulfPub corroboration or contradiction.

Haradh (Al-Ahsa, southern Ghawar, Eastern Province) to 'Uthmaniyah Gas Plant (central Ghawar, Eastern Province), both named as endpoints in OGJ.

Deep-fill: GEM Capacity was blank. Both OGJ articles (and Gulf Oil & Gas) state Haradh GOSP-3 produces 140 MMscfd of associated gas transported by this pipeline to Uthmaniyah — the design throughput at 2006 commissioning. Tier medium because the sources likely share a single Aramco announcement and 140 MMscfd is the GOSP gas output rather than a stated line 'capacity'.

Haradh GOSP-3 and its associated infrastructure are wholly a Saudi Aramco development; Owner Saudi Aramco 100% confirmed. (Length [ref] and Diameter [ref] left UNRESOLVED — 124 km and 24/32 in are not independently corroborated; sources give only ~160 km combined to Abqaiq + Uthmaniyah.)

routes.corridor_desc: Runs north along the Ghawar field trend in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province: from the Haradh area (southernmost Ghawar production area, near Haradh town ~24.14N/49.07E, GOSP-3) northward past the Hawiyah production area to the 'Uthmaniyah production area / Uthmaniyah Gas Plant in central Ghawar. Endpoints are named and firm (Haradh town well-located; Uthmaniyah gas plant location approximate to ~25.05N/49.28E within the central Ghawar Uthmaniyah production area). Ghawar's production areas from south to north are Haradh -> Hawiyah -> Uthmaniyah -> Shedgum -> Ain Dar, which fixes the corridor orientation; the ~124 km GEM length is consistent with the Haradh->Uthmaniyah span but the exact routing between the two is not surveyed here.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints (Haradh GOSP-3 -> Uthmaniyah Gas Plant) are explicitly named in OGJ. Haradh coordinate (24.14N/49.07E) is the well-known Haradh town location; Uthmaniyah Gas Plant coordinate (25.05N/49.28E) is APPROXIMATE, placed within the central-Ghawar Uthmaniyah production area (no surveyed plant coordinate sourced) — not fabricated to false precision. Corridor orientation is well constrained by the known N-S ordering of Ghawar production areas. No intermediate waypoints sourced; exact route left for a routes-repo branch.
